_about: The bill of materials the linter reads. Rules 2, 3, 4 and 5 of the volume are mechanical claims about parts, headers and voltages, and until this file existed they were prose that thirteen labs depended on and nothing could check. Every entry below is taken from a lab's own kit line and from the rule box in the front matter, not from the inventory of any one bench.
_why_json_and_not_yaml: The book toolchain is stdlib Python and has no requirements file. YAML would make a parser the repository's first third-party dependency, for one small table. JSON parses with the standard library, refuses a trailing comma loudly rather than guessing, and carries its commentary in note fields that the linter can print.

_schema.hosts: id to name, header type and logic volts. A host owns a header; it does not claim one.
_schema.parts: id to name, kind, the header it fits, whether it claims that header exclusively, its logic volts, whether it is one of the six instruments of rule 5, and the labs that use it. The labs list is redundant with the labs block and is checked against it, which is the point: a lab that quietly drops a part fails the check.
_schema.labs: id to the hosts it permits, the parts seated on each host's header, and the parts attached by USB, flying leads or a rail rather than seated.

nanopi.name: NanoPi NEO Air
nanopi.note: Rule 3. A 24-pin header that cannot accept any 40-pin HAT.

mcc118.name: MCC 118 DAQ HAT
mcc118.note: Also one of the six instruments of rule 5. Its analogue inputs are limited to plus or minus 10.1 V, which is a separate limit from the 3.3 V logic rule.

lcd_a.name: Waveshare 3.5 inch RPi LCD (A)
lcd_a.note: Mates pins 1 to 26 and has no pass-through. Whether its carrier PCB also overhangs pins 27 to 40 is unmeasured, and P19 is blocked until it is.

dsi_touch.name: official Raspberry Pi touchscreen
dsi_touch.note: Rule 2 names this explicitly: the DISPLAY connector is not the 40-pin header, so this may sit beside a HAT.

stwin.name: STEVAL-STWINBX1 STWIN.box
stwin.note: A USB-C device, not a shield and not a HAT.

iks5a1.name: X-NUCLEO-IKS5A1
iks5a1.note: Stacks one at a time. P08's kit line says with the IKS4A1 removed, which is rule 5 in practice.

ppk2.name: nRF Power Profiler Kit II
ppk2.note: Deliberately not one of the six. Rule 5 counts the physics under test, and the PPK2 measures current rather than a phenomenon, so it may sit in a lab beside one of the six.

ttl_cable.name: Renkforce USB/TTL cable, PL2303HX
ttl_cable.note: Sealed moulding. Its 3.3 V logic level is documented by the vendor and has not been measured on this bench.

pow_bb.name: SBC-POW-BB breadboard supply
pow_bb.note: Rule 4. A labelled rail splitter that can also present 5 V, which is why no jumper may run from its 5 V rail to any host header pin.

lk_led10.name: Joy-it LK-LED10 module
lk_led10.note: Carries its own resistor. Signal and ground only, the signal pin is the anode side, and a pin driven high is lit.

P07.note: The kit line permits either Pi as the recording host.

P13.note: Two modems at once, and the only lab that is legal solely because the two HATs sit on two different hosts. The draft pairing this volume rejects is both on one Pi.

P15.note: Any Pi or NanoPi host. Run on the Pi 3 Model B Rev 1.2 on Friday 2 October 2026.

P18.note: The shield and the second console are both optional in the kit line, and are listed so that rule 5 still counts the instrument if they are fitted.

P19.note: The sensor is on flying leads and claims no header, but the panel covers pins 1 to 26 and the sensor has nowhere to go. That is a spatial conflict this file cannot express, and it is why the lab is blocked.
